findings.scenario: S30 (ingestion) — the live Sourcify fetch during the first REAL capture
findings.observed: the ingest endpoint (the deprecated Sourcify `files/any/{chain}/{addr}`) returned HTTP 503, so every live fetch resolved `unavailable` — the pipeline would have shipped 0 REAL tiers
findings.rootCause: Sourcify migrated its server API; the `files/any` endpoint is deprecated/overloaded
findings.fix: fromSourcify was pointed at the Sourcify v2 API (`GET /v2/contract/{chain}/{addr}?fields=sources,compilation`) with the v2 response shape (match=exact_match -> REAL; a non-exact match -> SAMPLE; a non-Solidity language -> unavailable); the hermetic mock was updated to the v2 shape
findings.retest: the live fetch of the aave-v3 Pool + compound-v3 cUSDCv3 -> exact_match REAL; contract_ingest green on the v2 shape; two consecutive clean runs identical

findings.scenario: S29 (the render path) — the coverage helper was not exported from the barrel
findings.observed: the battery reddened with 'Export named contractCoverage not found in module src/contract/index.ts' — the REAL-coverage count broke the whole contract_registry_real file load
findings.rootCause: contractCoverage was added to registry.ts but not re-exported from src/contract/index.ts (the test imports from the barrel)
findings.fix: contractCoverage added to the index.ts barrel re-export
findings.retest: contract_registry_real green; the Shelf coverage line renders; two consecutive clean runs identical

findings.scenario: S25 (the REAL tier ceiling) — proxy vs implementation honesty
findings.observed: the captured verified sources for the shelf incumbents are the deployed PROXY contracts (aave-v3 Pool, compound-v3 cUSDCv3), NOT the implementation logic; a naive reader could over-read a REAL FLAGGED proxy tier as a full-logic audit
findings.rootCause: Sourcify EXACT-match resolves the source at the deployed address (the proxy); the implementation is a separate address
findings.fix: the scope is SURFACED, not silent — each finding names its contract (proxy-level vs OZ-primitive) transparently; the ceiling ('a structural screen over verified source — not a full audit, never safe') holds harder on REAL; D10 records that the captured sources are the deployed proxies (an upgradeable admin proxy IS a real counterparty surface the analyzer correctly flags), not impl-logic audits; the coverage count is honest
findings.retest: the REAL FLAGGED tier names its findings by contract; the safety guard rejects a 'safe' claim; the ceiling label present in Simple + Pro; two consecutive clean runs identical

convergence.battery: 703 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 112 files (704 tests), byte-identical across two consecutive runs; deterministic (the offline battery forces the AI keys empty, so the Operator-gated live-AI test ask_live.test.ts skips — the surviving 1 skip, P3)

postSprint: the contract axis is now EXERCISED on real data: the verified-build pipeline (keyless-first Sourcify v2 ingestion -> deterministic forge build-capture -> the content-hashed registry) scored the FIRST REAL tiers on the live shelf — 4 of the 7 applicable pools (aave-v3 USDC/USDT/DAI via the aave-v3 Pool; compound-v3 USDC via cUSDCv3), each REAL FLAGGED (the upgradeable-admin-proxy surface, honestly a screen not an audit), the other 3 applicable pools honestly UNVERIFIED. The REAL/SAMPLE wall holds (a SAMPLE/absent build never a clean tier); the tier is material:false (a REAL FLAGGED never moved a SOLID verdict); the pipeline is off the hot loop (capture-time; the render reads the committed content-hashed registry, zero compilation); no model, no scrape, no new npm dep. Every Contract-Truth finding (V1-V5) is closed (V5 CLOSED — the real integration).
